text:
Sam: thinking out loud — can we try a descheduling hierarchy so heavy tenants get soft-descheduled before we start evicting microbatches?
Maya: like a two-tier descheduler? soft -> hard?
Sam: yeah. soft deschedule reduces coalesce pressure by delaying admit, hard deschedule would forcibly drain tenant windows.
Raj: what's the ctl surface between scheduler and prefetch layer? i.e., who signals warmup vs fallback path?
Priya: scheduler should expose a small enum: {OK, SOFT_DESCHEDULE, HARD_DESCHEDULE, REJECT}. prefetch reads that and opts into aggressive kv-warm/warmth or fallback to small-model path.
Alex: +1 on enum, but worry about coupling. prefetch already has model selection logic — we don't want scheduler to make model choices. it should only provide latency/cost hints.
Maya: agreed. keep model selection in prefetch. scheduler hints: deadline_slack_ms, deschedule_level, and prefer_low_state boolean.
Raj: can we quantify impact? if soft deschedule delays admission by 15–30ms we might avoid an eviction that costs p99+500ms due to kv-warm.
Sam: early sim: for 10% heavy tenants, soft deschedule reduced eviction count by ~35% and p99 for others dropped ~80ms. but p50 slightly worse for the soft-descheduled requests.
Priya: tradeoff is fairness vs latency. soft-deschedule trades small latency for one group to keep overall SLOs. need SLA knob per tenant.
Alex: also need to avoid oscillation: tenant toggles between soft and hard quickly. add hysteresis window and stable-time threshold (e.g., 30s).
Maya: + add token-bucket style budget per tenant for soft-deschedule credits. once budget exhausted, escalate to hard.
Sam: how do we surface observability? want a per-tenant timeline: admission_decision, deschedule_level, queue_depth, kv_hit_rate, observed_latency.
Raj: add a lightweight event stream (batch of events per second) to Console. don't flood prometheus.
Priya: fallback policy integration: prefetch can choose reduced-kv fetch (only first n layers) or smaller model variant. scheduler should publish a compatibility list for fallbacks.
Alex: compatibility list is important. we already have compatible_variants in model-catalog — reuse that table rather than duplicating logic.
Maya: implementation plan: 1) define scheduler hint proto (enum + slack_ms + stable_window) 2) wire hint into admission path 3) prefetch reads hint and picks fallback variant if prefer_low_state true 4) telemetry + canary.
Sam: scoping: implement soft deschedule + hysteresis first, leave hard deschedule for follow-up.
Raj: question: queue isolation — will soft-deschedule require per-tenant subqueues? or just admission-throttling?
Priya: admission-throttling is simpler initially. subqueues would help isolation but need refactor of queueing surface. prefer progressive rollout.
Alex: on the API surface, expose tenant-level policy in Dedicated config: deschedule_budget, deschedule_thresholds. default off for hosted.
Maya: risk: misconfigured budgets could starve tenants. add a safety: global_min_admit_rate to ensure small throughput.
Sam: action items: Sam -> proto + design doc; Maya -> simulation harness changes; Raj -> Console event schema; Priya -> prefetch fallback hooks; Alex -> config + rollout plan.
CI-bot: deploy-checks pending: lint ok, unit tests missing for proto (Sam).
Sam: noted. will add unit tests.
Priya: can we add a small example snippet for the hint proto?
Sam: sure — copying here:
```
// scheduler_hint.proto (sketch)
message SchedulerHint {
  enum Level { OK = 0; SOFT = 1; HARD = 2; REJECT = 3; }
  Level level = 1;
  int32 deadline_slack_ms = 2; // positive relaxes deadline
  int32 stable_window_s = 3; // hysteresis
  bool prefer_low_state = 4; // hint to prefetch
}
```
Maya: looks good. keep fields minimal.
Raj: one more concern — cold-start collateral: soft-deschedule might amplify cold-starts if many prefetched caches are starved. need simulation to include kvcache heat decay.
Maya: yep will add heat-decay param and synthetic traces.
Alex: timeline? aim for spec + proto this week, simulation next week, small canary in 2–3 weeks.
Sam: thanks everyone. will draft doc and ping for review. :thumbsup:
